key_insight: RTDMD shows that minimizing KL to a reward-tilted teacher distribution for few-step flow generators decomposes into a distribution-matching term plus a reward-weighted correction, enabling a practical two-stage distillation + reward-guided fine-tuning pipeline that yields fast samplers aligned with preferences.
problem_solved: Aligning highly compressed/few-step generative samplers (distilled diffusion/flow models) with human preferences or external reward signals without sacrificing sample quality or speed.
method: Construct a reward-tilted teacher distribution by reweighting high-quality generative outputs with a reward model or preference signal.
Stage 1: Distribution-matching distillation — fit a few-step flow generator to the reward-tilted teacher via KL minimization (supervised distillation component).

Stage 2: Reward-guided fine-tuning — apply a reward-weighted / RL-style correction to the distilled generator to further align outputs with the reward while preserving sample fidelity and inference speed.
impact: Provides a practical recipe to produce fast, few-step generative samplers that better reflect human preferences or task rewards, improving deployability of aligned image generators with minimal inference cost.
